behavioral_effects: All four governance hook commands are location-independent; a drifted shell can no longer silently disable the read gate or stop-check via spawn errors
compatibility_impact: Hooks now run identically regardless of the session shell's working directory; no behavior change when cwd is the repo root
limitations: A spawn-level failure still cannot announce itself (nothing runs to do the announcing) - this fix removes the known spawn-failure cause rather than adding an announcer; the CI gate smoke step remains the backstop for the scripts themselves
reason: The Stop hook failed to spawn when the session shell's working directory sat in backend/ - every governance hook command used repo-relative paths, so any cwd drift silently disabled the read gate and stop-check with a spawn error instead of a designed, announced degradation. Hooks must be location-independent: Claude Code provides CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR to hook processes, and anchoring the four governance hook commands to it removes the entire failure class
rollback: git revert restores relative paths and the cwd-drift failure class
security_impact: None - same commands, absolute anchoring via the CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR variable Claude Code provides to hook processes

validators_run.evidence_ref: hook scripts are loaded by file path in tests, unaffected by command-string changes; verified live instead - both hook kinds executed correctly from a deliberately drifted backend/ cwd, the exact condition that produced the spawn failure
